z-m-17-03.topic: Volume of sphere: relation among sphere, cone, and cylinder volumes
z-m-17-03.goal: Estimate relation among sphere, cone, cylinder volumes before calculation; update estimate when measurement result arrive, sort out exact ratio, and estimate volume multiplier when lengths double.

z-m-17-03.s.s2.model.1: A=36π and C=54π cm³, so A÷C=2/3. Sphere fit exactly in cylinder but corners empty; e fill two-thirds, no be half. Sua guess need correction.

z-m-17-04.title: Wetin we need know to find angle between bisectors of two angles?
z-m-17-04.goal: Tell apart information needed from missing info to decide angle formed by two bisectors; make different cases with same value; explain condition for “always 90°.”
z-m-17-04.material: Rays OA, OB, OC start from O. OB between OA and OC, so ∠AOC=∠AOB+∠BOC, and ∠AOC more than 0° and at most 180°. OM bisect ∠AOB; ON bisect ∠BOC. Find size of ∠MON.

z-m-17-04.s.s1.prompt: We wan decide ∠MON. Choose all information where knowing only that lets you decide ∠MON.

z-m-17-04.s.s1.r.b: Check whether knowing both angles let you decide all four small angles formed by two bisectors.
z-m-17-04.s.s1.r.c: Here only ratio known, no sizes. Compare ∠MON when ∠AOB=20° and when e 40°.
z-m-17-04.s.s1.r.d: You only know two angles equal. Check whether that decide if each 40° or 70°.
z-m-17-04.s.s1.r.e: Find why you no need know ∠AOB and ∠BOC separately by looking at angles making ∠MON.
z-m-17-04.s.s1.explain: OM and ON bisect ∠AOB and ∠BOC, so ∠MON=½∠AOB+½∠BOC=½∠AOC. So knowing both angles or just sum ∠AOC enough. Knowing one angle, only ratio, or only that two equal no enough.

z-m-17-04.s.s2.hint.1: Add small angles made by bisectors directly and check total 70°.
z-m-17-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Both angles positive and ∠AOC at most 180°.

z-m-17-04.s.s2.fail.c2: ∠MON no be 70°. Add small angles from both bisectors and check.
z-m-17-04.s.s2.explain: If a+b=140, then ∠MON=70°. For example, 40° and 100° give 20°+50°=70°; 70° and 70° give 35°+35°=70°.

z-m-17-05.title: Is middle of two classes’ means the overall mean?
z-m-17-05.topic: Mean: mean of two groups combined
z-m-17-05.goal: Decide whether overall mean can be found from class means alone; find student-number combinations with same overall mean; use numbers to explain why mean lean toward group with more students.
z-m-17-05.material: Class A and B do same math test. A mean 70 points, B mean 80. Find overall mean for both classes together. Each class get at least 1 and at most 40 students. Doyun say, “(70+80)÷2=75, so overall mean 75 points.”

z-m-17-01.thinking.2: Explaining why 2 quantities change differently with the same variable
z-m-17-01.prereq.0: Circle circumference and area, and how sector arc length and area directly proportional to its central angle (grade 7 level)
z-m-17-01.prereq.1: π (pi) na ratio of circle circumference to diameter
z-m-17-01.s.s1.prompt: Before calculating, choose wetin you think now about Mina statement.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine 2 decorations with same ribbon length. Think about when their radii equal and when dem different.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.hint.1: Think wetin must happen to central angle for arc length to stay same when radius increase.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.o.a: Always correct. If ribbon length same, decorations get same shape
z-m-17-01.s.s1.r.a: You think once ribbon length set, radius and central angle get only one pair. Since radius and central angle together decide arc length, check whether their values fit differ but arc length still same.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.o.b: Always wrong. Two decorations with same ribbon length always get different areas
z-m-17-01.s.s1.r.b: This judgment forget 2 decorations fit get same radius. Check wetin happen to both decorations if their radii same too.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.o.c: We no fit tell now. We fit judge only if dem give central angle
z-m-17-01.s.s1.r.c: You think judgment hard unless dem give values. But question like 'is it always the same?' fit be tested by making examples, without choosing one fixed value.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.o.d: E depend on the case. Sometimes e same, sometimes e different
z-m-17-01.s.s1.r.d: You think you must find which cases make am same and which make am different. Test those cases with examples.
z-m-17-01.s.s1.explain: At first, 'it depends on the case' na the best judgment. If radius same, central angle also same and decorations identical; but if radius different, dem fit differ. Now make examples and check am.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 sector decorations with ribbon length 6π cm but different radii. (radius r cm, central angle x°)
z-m-17-01.s.s2.hint.0: First decide the relation between r and x wey make arc length expression equal 6π.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.hint.1: Choose r, find x, then calculate arc length directly to confirm say e be 6π.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.ok.c1: Radius positive and central angle greater than 0° and less than 360°.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.fail.c1: For am to be sector, radius must pass 0 and central angle must pass 0° but below 360°.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Arc length no be 6π cm. Put r and x inside arc length formula and check whether e equal 6π.
z-m-17-01.s.s2.explain: With radius 6 cm and central angle 180°, area na 18π cm²; with radius 12 cm and central angle 90°, area na 36π cm²; with radius 18 cm and central angle 60°, area na 54π cm². Even with same ribbon length, different radius mean different area.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.prompt: Answer Mina. Choose 2 decorations you make above, compare their areas, and explain why areas differ although ribbon length same.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.hint.0: Among your decorations, choose the 2 wey radii differ pass and write each area.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.hint.1: For both decorations, compare how many times bigger radius become and how many times bigger area become.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.placeholder: e.g., The decoration with radius ... has ...
z-m-17-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You use numbers compare radius, central angle, and area for both decorations?
z-m-17-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Apart from saying 'the area differs,' you write the reason (say the radius different)?
z-m-17-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You also think wetin happen when ribbon length and radius both same?
z-m-17-01.s.s3.model.0: Even with same ribbon length, area different. The decoration with radius 6 cm and central angle 180° has area 18π, but the decoration with radius 12 cm and central angle 90° has 36π, double. When radius increase, area increase even if central angle decrease.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.model.1: The idea say “always same” wrong. Even with same 6π cm ribbon, radius 9 get central angle 120° and area 27π, while radius 18 get central angle 60° and area 54π, so dem different. Na decorations with same radius get same area.
z-m-17-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: This answer connect with the first judgment, 'it depends on the case.'
z-m-17-01.s.s3.model.2: Sector area = ½ × r × arc length = 3πr, so even if arc lengths same, bigger radius mean bigger area.

z-m-17-02.title: Finding the wrong line for solution about angle between clock hands
z-m-17-02.topic: Angle size and units: angle between clock hands
z-m-17-02.goal: Find and fix the wrong line in solution for angle between clock hands, and explain say when both hands move, set each hand position separately to match the time.
z-m-17-02.material:
For analog clock face, 12 numbers dey spaced equally, and dem measure angles clockwise from 12 direction. Clock accurate and both hands turn at steady rate. Hour hand make one full turn in 12 hours, and minute hand make one full turn in 60 minutes. Minjae try find the smaller angle between hour and minute hands at 3:20, and solve am like this.
1) One full turn na 360° and 12 numbers dey, so space between numbers na 30°.
2) Minute hand make one turn in 60 minutes, so e move 6° each minute, and at 20 minutes e don move 120° from 12.
3) Hour hand point to 3, so e dey 90° from 12.
4) Angle between both hands na 120° − 90° = 30°.
5) So angle between hour and minute hands at 3:20 na 30°.
z-m-17-02.thinking.0: Checking every solution line with the real situation
z-m-17-02.thinking.1: Finding the wrong line and solving again with corrected value
z-m-17-02.thinking.2: Explaining the reason for error to another person
z-m-17-02.prereq.0: Expressing angle size in degrees (°) and knowing full turn na 360°
z-m-17-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose one wrong line for Minjae solution.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.hint.0: Match hand positions written in each line one by one with real clock at 3:20.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.hint.1: Draw clock at exactly 3 and clock at 3:20, then compare which picture match hand positions in each line.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.line.0: One full turn na 360° and clock get 12 numbers, so one number space na 30°.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.line.1: Minute hand make one turn in 60 minutes, so e move 6° per minute; after 20 minutes e don move 120° from 12 direction.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.line.2: Hour hand dey point to 3, so e be 90° from 12 direction.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.line.4: So angle between hour and minute hands at 3:20 na 30°.
z-m-17-02.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. At 3:20 hour hand no remain at 3; while minute hand go round for 20 minutes, hour hand move forward small too. Hour hand make one turn (360°) in 12 hours, so 30° each hour, and move 10° more in 20 minutes, making am 100° from 12 direction. Lines 4 and 5 use line 3 value as e be, so calculation correct but result change. [3 3 20 3 20 360 12 30 20 10 100 12 4 5 3]
z-m-17-02.s.s2.prompt: If you correct Minjae solution, how many degrees be smaller angle between hands at 3:20?
z-m-17-02.s.s2.hint.0: First find how many degrees hour hand move in one hour (60 minutes).
z-m-17-02.s.s2.hint.1: Use that value to find angle hour hand move in 20 minutes, update its position, and compare with minute hand position.
z-m-17-02.s.s2.r.a: You answer only angle (10°) hour hand move in extra 20 minutes. Angle between hands come from comparing positions of hour and minute hands.
z-m-17-02.s.s2.r.b: You compare both hand positions again, including hour hand movement in 20 minutes.
z-m-17-02.s.s2.r.c: You carry over first solution as-is, treating hour hand as if e stay at 3.
z-m-17-02.s.s2.r.d: You read hour hand position (angle from 12 direction) as angle between both hands. You need compare am with minute hand position.
z-m-17-02.s.s2.explain: Hour hand at 100° and minute hand at 120°, so angle between dem na 20°. Another way: minute hand move 5.5° per minute faster than hour hand. At 3, minute hand 90° behind; in 20 minutes e catch up 110°, so e dey ahead by 20°.
z-m-17-02.s.s3.prompt: Write note to Minjae. Explain how line 3 suppose change and why.
z-m-17-02.s.s3.hint.0: Compare if hour hand position same at exactly 3 and at 3:20.
z-m-17-02.s.s3.hint.1: Use hour hand degrees per hour to find how many degrees e move in 20 minutes.
z-m-17-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you write in numbers how much farther hour hand move from 3?
z-m-17-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you explain how angle between hands change after adding that amount?
z-m-17-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you consider why Minjae may write line 3 that way?
z-m-17-02.s.s3.model.0: Hour hand move small while minute hand turn, so at 3:20 e dey at 100°, 10° pass 3. So change line 3 to 100°, and angle become 120°−100°=20°.
z-m-17-02.s.s3.model.1: Hour hand move 30° per hour, so 10° more in 20 minutes. Line 3 suppose be 90°+10°=100°, making angle 20°, no be 30°. [30 20 10 3 90 10 100 20 30]
z-m-17-02.s.s3.model.2: Hour hand move 0.5 degrees per minute, so e move 10 degrees more in 20 minutes. Correct line 3 to 100 degrees. [0.5 20 10 3 100]
z-m-17-02.s.s3.modelNote.2: Answer explained with movement per minute.

z-m-17-07.title: If scores change by same rule, how mean and score gaps go change?
z-m-17-07.topic: Mean, median, range: when scores change by fixed rule
z-m-17-07.goal: Learn how representative values and spread change when you add same number or multiply all values by same number, and make adjustment rules wey meet conditions, then compare dem.
z-m-17-07.material: Math test hard, so mean low. Teacher wan change all students scores by same rule. Original scores for 7 students na 35, 50, 55, 55, 65, 70, 90 points, and mean na 60 points, median na 55 points, mode na 55 points, and gap between highest and lowest score na 55 points. Adjusted score na 'original score × p + q' (p na number greater than 0), and score no fit pass 100 points.
z-m-17-07.thinking.1: Designing rule wey meet plenty conditions together
z-m-17-07.prereq.0: Finding mean, median, mode, and gap between biggest and smallest data values
z-m-17-07.prereq.1: Putting numbers inside expression with letters (p × score + q) to find the answer
z-m-17-07.s.s1.prompt: Rule A: Add 8 points to every student score. Choose everything wey stay same after change.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.hint.0: Add 8 to the 7 original scores and write the 7 new ones.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.hint.1: Compare mean, median, mode, and highest-lowest gap for old and new scores.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.r.a: Check if you remember say when all scores rise by 8, score total increase.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.o.b: Middle value when the 7 scores dey in order (median)
z-m-17-07.s.s1.r.b: Think whether middle score also rise by the same 8 points.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.o.c: Gap between highest and lowest scores
z-m-17-07.s.s1.r.c: See wetin happen to gap between 2 scores when both rise by same amount.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.o.d: The score wey appear most among the 7 students (mode)
z-m-17-07.s.s1.r.d: Think whether the score wey appear most still appear most after rise by 8.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.o.e: Who rank how high, the score order
z-m-17-07.s.s1.r.e: Check whether adding same points to everybody change who higher.
z-m-17-07.s.s1.explain: If you add 8 points to every score, the mean 60 points → 68 points, the median 55 points → 63 points, and the mode 55 points → 63 points, all rise by 8 points. Score gaps stay same, so gap between highest and lowest scores (55 points) and score order no change.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.prompt: Set adjustment rule as 'original score × p + q.' Find 3 different rules (p, q) wey meet all these. ① Mean after adjustment exactly 75 points. ② Highest score after adjustment no pass 100 points. ③ Gap between highest and lowest scores after adjustment at least half the original (55 points).
z-m-17-07.s.s2.hint.0: Mean na the result when you apply same rule to original mean of 60 points. Find the relation p and q need so answer become 75.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.hint.1: Choose p, find q, then apply rule to highest 90 and lowest 35 to check both conditions.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.ok.c1: p greater than 0, so score order stay.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.fail.c1: p must pass 0 to keep score order.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.fail.c2: The mean after adjusting is not 75 points. Check whether same rule on original mean 60 give 75.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.fail.c3: Applying rule to original highest score 90 make am pass 100 points.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.ok.c4: Gap between highest and lowest scores at least 27.5 points.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.fail.c4: Gap between highest and lowest after adjustment below 27.5 points. Apply rule to the original 2 scores (90 points, 35 points) and find gap.
z-m-17-07.s.s2.explain: With p=0.8, q=27, scores turn to 55, 67, 71, 71, 79, 83, 99 points, so mean na 75 points, highest score na 99 points, and gap na 44 points. With p=0.6, q=39, mean na 75 points, highest score na 93 points, and gap na 33 points. As p get smaller than 1, score gaps narrow, and q raise everything.
z-m-17-07.s.s3.prompt: Choose one rule you find and compare with rule A (add 8 points). Use numbers explain the gap between high and low score under each rule.

z-m-17-07.s.s3.hint.1: Compare new score gap with 55 and find how many times e be.

z-m-17-07.s.s3.model.0: I choose rule multiply by 0.8 and add 27 points. Highest score 90 points become 99 points and lowest 35 become 55 points, so their gap shrink from 55 points to 44 points. If you only add 8, gap stay 55 points, but with multiplication rule, score gaps narrow.
